spatial_claims.claim: C is a point on segment AB (between A and B)
D is on AB produced beyond B, so B lies between A and D; points are collinear in order A-C-B-D
B is a point on segment AD (consistent with A-C-B-D collinear order)

configuration_map: All points lie on a single straight line in the order A — C — B — D, with BD = CB. Point C is an arbitrary cut of AB; point D is constructed on AB produced beyond B so that BD equals CB. The full segment AD = AB + BD = AB + BC. No points off the line are constructed; no triangles, circles, or angles are involved. The proof operates entirely through algebraic area identities (2.4 and 2.7) applied to this collinear configuration.
pass_reason: The proof's spatial claims are limited to collinear point positions on a single line (A-C-B-D with BD=CB), all trivially and mutually consistent. The core reasoning is purely algebraic manipulation of area identities from Propositions 2.4 and 2.7, with no angle decompositions, no inside/outside claims, no ray orderings, and no opportunity for spatial configuration contradictions.
